source.name: Synthetic sweeping-generalization development passages
source.notes: Independent synthetic passages for the accepted sweeping-generalization check.

snippets: Audiences hate being reminded that a film is a constructed object; they want the director to disappear.
Nobody comes to a cinema hoping to think about the labor that produced the picture.
Jazz listeners enjoy being difficult to please.
they'll feel we have taken away the thing that sets them apart
Solo travelers are solitary people by temperament, so they won't enjoy a shared breakfast or an introduction to the other guests.
Their decision to book alone tells us how much conversation they are willing to tolerate.
Amateur cyclists care more about their equipment than their fitness.
The carbon frame gives them the excuse they need to avoid admitting they should train harder.
Anyone visiting Paris is looking for romance, whether they admit it or not.
Retired voters long for the country they grew up in, and every election is an opportunity for them to recover it.
Every athlete is chasing the approval they missed out on as a child.
Freelancers value independence above security.
Offering a permanent contract will feel like a loss of freedom to them, even if the salary doubles their current income.
Voters only listen when a politician promises to put money in their pockets.
We understand, as parents, that a difficult book is a threat to a child's confidence.
Give families something easier and they will thank us for protecting their children.
People treat a friendship as disposable once it asks anything inconvenient of them.
Everyone is measuring what they get back, even when they call it unconditional affection.
Everyone who buys a smartwatch wants their private life turned into a competition.
Everybody wants a pill rather than the inconvenience of changing their routine.
Programmers would rather rebuild a working tool than admit somebody else solved the problem.
Children learn only when they are having fun
University students see attendance requirements as an insult.
They believe paying fees gives them the right to ignore any teaching that doesn't immediately interest them.
People don't support environmental measures when they have to sacrifice anything themselves.
The public enthusiasm for greener streets disappears the moment walking is involved.
Refugees want to leave their old identity behind and start again.
Workers care about the size of the pay packet, not the language of the agreement.
they will stop worrying about shift control
Local people resent travelers who stay for just a day.
They see a short visit as taking something from the town without giving anything back to it.
We all turn to music because words alone cannot express our feelings.
People who order steak well done are afraid of trying anything new.
That confirms what people want from software: a score that tells them they are doing better than their neighbors.
everyone cares more about being ahead than about keeping a copy of the underlying data
Accountants are uncomfortable with unstructured conversation; they need every social activity to have a measurable purpose.
A quiet walk would leave them feeling that the morning had been wasted.
Travelers become helpless as soon as something goes wrong; they want an authority figure to take every decision away from them.
Being told what to do is what people find reassuring in an unfamiliar airport.
Working-class visitors find abstraction pretentious
For Italians, a broken strand of spaghetti feels like an insult to the family.
Customers love a story about a grandmother because it makes them believe the food is honest.
They will accept a higher price as soon as they imagine a family kitchen.
People with chronic pain become experts at exaggerating symptoms to be taken seriously.
Who doesn't want a promotion?
Staff who turn one down are protecting themselves from the disappointment of failing
Village residents don't welcome newcomers until they have proved they belong.
Isn't winning the only thing any of us remembers?
The juniors will forget a friendly coach long before they forget the chance to lift a trophy.
Children reject vegetables because they want to be in control of the table.
Women read historical fiction to escape the disappointments of ordinary life
What these readers want is somewhere more elegant to live for an hour or two.
Parents respond to vaccination advice emotionally rather than rationally; statistics just make them dig in.
A warm message is the only language they understand when their own children are involved.
Commuters judge every public project by how much time it saves them personally
Anyone shopping for a phone considers a repaired handset second best
Customers need to see untouched boxes first because the idea of previous ownership makes them uncomfortable.
Novelists are jealous of anyone who finishes a book faster than they do.
Musicians regard punctuality as a threat to spontaneity, and a strict schedule makes them feel that the performance has already been compromised.
Many older users are frightened of changing anything on a computer.
They regard an unfamiliar menu as evidence that they have broken the machine.
Office workers interpret a private desk as a sign of importance, and they resent anyone who gets one before them.
people are keeping a mental ranking of whose furniture says they matter most
We all relax the moment we hear our own language abroad.
Many people who volunteer are really looking for an audience for their goodness.
Private acts of kindness can't give them the public approval they need.
Business owners see a public consultation as an obstacle to getting things done.
They will support whatever lets the planning committee finish faster, regardless of the proposal itself.
Parents at junior sport see their children as future professionals, so they interpret every minute on the bench as a personal insult.
Collectors want a work that other people cannot have.
People in regional offices always feel overlooked by headquarters
Doctors resent patients who arrive with internet research; they feel their authority slipping as soon as a website is mentioned.
Patients hear a second opinion as an admission that medicine has failed.
Runners are addicted to proving they can endure pain.
Offer them a comfortable training programme and they will assume it cannot possibly be making them stronger.
Traditional fans believe that any change to the stadium is an attack on the club's history.
Office workers buy sweet pastries because they see breakfast as a reward for having to get up and go to work.
Every sibling keeps score of who their parents loved the most.
The average internet user treats privacy as someone else's problem until a photograph leaks.
People who use Linux see every technical inconvenience as a badge of honor.
Readers resent an ending that makes them decide what happened.
Tourists want a photograph of a place more than they want to understand it.
It's the same in every neighborhood: homeowners care about property prices, renters care about convenience.
Isn't a slim body what we all really want?
that shared ambition
New mothers instinctively distrust advice from anyone who hasn't had a baby.
Isn't eating together what makes us all feel at home?
Even the most reserved guest wants to be pulled into a noisy conversation over a shared dish.
Who doesn't want their children nearby as they grow older?
Parents who encourage a move abroad are hiding their disappointment to avoid looking selfish in front of the family.
Backpackers are suspicious of comfort; they need a trip to feel difficult before they consider it a real experience.
Teachers regard silence as proof that a lesson is going well.
Don't we all feel safer when an app asks for a password?
People who watch women's sport are looking for a moral statement as much as a match.
City people regard a quiet village as a place that needs improving.
Football supporters would rather blame the referee than admit their team played badly.
Americans abroad expect every meal to arrive exactly as it would at home.
They read a small portion as poor service
Former competitors can't enjoy a casual activity without turning it into a contest.
An only child expects every conversation to revolve around them.
Families hold on to old arguments because resentment is how they keep a sense of belonging.
Many people who choose expensive wine are buying social approval rather than flavor. They need the rest of the table to see how much the bottle costs.
An employee's first instinct is to hide a mistake. That's human nature
people will conceal whatever they can
Children are natural performers who crave an audience
We all know that nobody really trusts their local council.
People who leave their hometown are ashamed of where they came from
Developers hate reaching for a mouse
Guests judge how much you value them by where you put their chair
Island residents measure outsiders by whether they can handle rough weather without complaining.
Most academics are motivated by the prospect of seeing their name in print. Appeals to student benefit won't persuade them
We all want our boss to notice when we stay late.
People who ask for plant-based alternatives want everyone nearby to know they are making an ethical choice.
Adult learners are embarrassed to ask basic questions because they feel they should already know the answers. They will quietly struggle rather than approach a librarian.
Young professionals see a job as a temporary stepping stone.
Older men will always put pride before asking for help.
Every parent secretly wants their child to finish top of the class.
Everyone loves the smell of bread coming out of an oven.
This is how patients think: if something is printed, it must be reliable.
Real home cooks never measure; they trust their senses instead.
People who take up running are trying to outrun something in their lives; the finish time is just the explanation they give friends.
People who stay single are protecting themselves from the risk of being known.
"People buy technology to impress other people."
The product page should therefore show the watch at a dinner party
"Freelancers hate being tied down," says the recruitment guide. That's why we should offer short contracts
"readers want justice, even in a love story."
an audience will feel cheated if the dishonest brother gets away with it
"Nobody wants to hear about risk when they're expecting a baby."
Most app users take a reminder as a sign that somebody cares.
Many parents choose a school to confirm the sort of family they believe they are.
They are buying a reflection of themselves as much as an education.
Employees tend to keep useful information to themselves because being indispensable feels safer than being helpful.
People tend to value a friendship by how quickly a message is answered.
They read the delay as a measure of how much they matter
what friends are waiting for is reassurance that they came first
